claims.text: arXiv cs.AI RSS timestamped the paper announcement at 2026-09-07T04:00:00Z.
The announcement was 22 hours 47 minutes 49 seconds old when the run began.
The arXiv submission history records v1 lodged at 2026-09-03T16:26:20Z.
The work is a preprint.
Harbor reports more than 80 adapters and a large evaluation covering 54 benchmarks, 6,627 tasks, eight models and 16 model-harness configurations.
The large evaluation used three trials per configuration, about 0.3 million trajectories, 226B tokens and more than US$300,000 compute.
Harbor's task abstraction covers instruction, environment, test and solution, reducing pairwise integration burden.
In this experiment the model fixed-effect range was 5.2 times the harness range, while harness and tool differences still affected behaviour.
After filtering and automated audit, a three-member human panel selected 100 tasks; the audit-and-fix loop then produced the final 82 spanning 29 benchmarks.
claims.sourceLocator: Paper sections 4.1-4.3 and launch selection funnel

claims.text: The paper reports roughly one-third of the hardest candidates across more than 30 benchmarks were rejected as broken rather than difficult.
The leading Harbor-Index 1.0 paper result was 28.0% for GPT-5.5 with Codex.
The 28.0% result is not a general deployment success rate because the index deliberately selects hard frontier tasks.
claims.sourceLocator: Paper sections 4.1-4.3 and launch purpose; no inference that the result lacks value

claims.text: After 12 benchmarks were selected, remaining model rankings correlated at least 0.7 with one selected benchmark.
For benchmarks with at least ten tasks, three representative tasks recovered system rankings at mean correlation about 0.923.
The redundancy findings support cheaper screening but do not prove a compact set represents a buyer's local tasks.
claims.sourceLocator: Paper sections 3.1 and 6 plus construct-validity boundary

claims.text: On 8 September 2026 the current README described 80 tasks, required at least five public trials per task for leaderboard submissions and pointed submissions to the Harbor-Index 1.3 leaderboard.
On 8 September 2026 the current config used three votes from Claude Opus 5 and documented earlier judge configurations.
The paper's 82-task result and current 80-task repository state are not interchangeable without a version.
claims.sourceLocator: Observed project-state difference; no claim that either release is wrong

claims.text: An independent SWE-bench audit found 7.8% of benchmark-passing patches failed developer tests, 29.6% differed behaviourally, and estimated inflation was 6.2 percentage points.
The SWE-bench audit supports the false-pass premise; Harbor's over-specified-verifier examples support the separate false-failure premise. The SWE-bench study does not evaluate Harbor.
claims.sourceLocator: s7 abstract for false passes; s2 section 4.1 for false failures; comparison boundary stated in article

claims.text: A systematic review used 29 expert reviewers across 445 benchmarks and found recurring construct-validity problems.
The lm-eval authors document sensitivity to setup, comparability, transparency and reproducibility.
Harbor-Index is appropriate as a versioned screening stage followed by representative local outcome testing.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from benchmark-purpose and reproducibility limits

claims.text: A reproducible agent result should retain task release, model, harness, verifier, attempts, tools, sandbox and budget.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from documented evaluation variables

claims.text: Harbor releases benchmark adapters, evaluation tooling and execution trajectories.
Harbor tasks can use a model judge, unit tests, exact matching or a threshold applied to a continuous metric.
The current README points leaderboard submissions to Harbor-Index 1.3.
Native harnesses allowed iterative correction, whereas Terminus-2 followed a one-way plan-to-execution-to-completion flow and lacked built-in image and web tools.
claims.sourceLocator: Section 3.4 and outcome discussion, HTML lines 258-264 and 296-298

claims.text: Specialised domains could resist cross-benchmark prediction, and the 54-benchmark experiment did not span every model, agent architecture or setting.
